newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble redenomination good for markets - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Rouble redenomination good for markets - analysts.

text.p: Russia's decision to issue a new rouble worth 1,000 old roubles starting next year is good news for equity and government securities investors, signalling Russia will stand by a stable rouble, analysts said on Monday.

"The big news on Russia is that Russia is a significantly different risk than it was six months ago," Mike Marrese, senior economist at Chase Investment Bank in London told Reuters Financial Television.
"That's the perception of investors, the perception of the IMF and the World Bank -- and that's most important for new investors."

Analysts agreed that the move to redenominate the rouble, which went into free-fall amid inflation rates over 1,000 percent in the early years of economic reform, would have a mainly psychological impact.
But they said the decision emphasised the success of the government's strict monetary policy in stabilising the rouble over the last year and a half.

"I think this tells us once again that the government plans to follow through with the same policies of fighting inflation, of keeping the rouble stable and so on," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's director of fixed income Vladimir Mersen.
"(Those policies) are very positive for the government securites market and equity market."
The government is forecasting inflation will dip to 11 percent this year after about 22 percent in 1996.

The announcement comes as yields on government bonds and treasury bills, currently around 18 percent annually, are dropping steadily lower, and analysts said the reassurance of a steady rouble over the next year would be welcomed by investors.
They said the announcement also came at an opportune moment for Russian corporations and banks seeking to tap international capital markets.
